clue.text: This cart carries heavy load three feet up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from the bottom to the top

parts.note: a yard is a length of three feet

explanation.surface: A description of a sturdy cart hauling a heavy load raised three feet off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three feet up' reads like a height, but it is a unit of length written backwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray is a low, strong flat cart without sides, traditionally used by brewers to haul barrels.

clue.text: Charm a Greek character hired out

parts.note: taken as written
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
to let a property is to hire it out

explanation.surface: A charming Greek man is employed for hire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' looks like a person, but in crosswords it almost always means a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a small trinket worn as a lucky charm, believed to ward off harm.

clue.text: Gaunt old American beneath fellow in saloon

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is held within it
in a down clue, what lies beneath comes later in the entry

parts.note: a saloon is a type of car, a sedan
the standard abbreviation for old
the United States, so American
any man's name can stand for a fellow

explanation.surface: A haggard elderly American sits below some man in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' suggests a Wild West bar, but it is the British word for a sedan car; a fellow sits inside it and the old American goes under.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadaverous literally means corpse-like, so it describes someone very thin, pale and gaunt.

clue.text: Repulsive party overturned fiscal promises

indicators.note: turning something over in a down clue flips its letters end to end

parts.note: a do is an informal party
IOUs are written promises to repay money

explanation.surface: A disgusting political party has reneged on its budget pledges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' and 'fiscal promises' suggest politics, but the party is a social one and the promises are IOUs.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious is a straightforward synonym meaning hateful or deeply offensive, arousing disgust.

clue.text: Call for rapid movement over Brexit problem?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over suggests flipping upwards so the reading runs backwards

parts.note: to page someone is to call for them over a system
a dart is a sudden quick movement

explanation.surface: Someone demands swift action to deal with a Brexit difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: an imbalance of imports and exports is one feared consequence of Britain leaving the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade gap is a deficit where imports exceed exports, an economic worry often linked to Brexit.

clue.text: Star not complete convert to compassionate eating?

indicators.note: a thing not complete is missing a part, here its final letter

parts.note: someone who adopts meat- and dairy-free eating out of compassion for animals

explanation.surface: A celebrity half-heartedly takes up kind, animal-friendly eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a celebrity convert but is the definition; 'convert to compassionate eating' is a whole phrase describing a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra, one of the most prominent in the northern sky.

clue.text: Six American spies surrounding rocky hill station

parts.note: six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: to surround something is to enclose it on all sides

parts.note: the Central Intelligence Agency of the US
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Half a dozen US agents surround a hill station in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hill station' reads as a colonial mountain resort, but the hill belongs to the wordplay and the station stands alone. Victoria is a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: London Victoria is one of the capital's busiest railway and coach terminals.

clue.text: As equipment in theatre idle sister wrecked

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, its parts thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lazy nun or nurse has damaged the props in a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests a stage, but here it is the operating theatre; a sister is also a senior nurse, which helps the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgical instruments in an operating room must be sterilised, made free of germs, before use.

clue.text: Robber one up holding atomic weapon the wrong way

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within one's grasp

parts.note: someone up on a horse or bike
A as in A-bomb, the atomic bomb

indicators.note: going the wrong way means running backwards

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A thief, one step ahead, is carrying a nuclear device backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One up' sounds like being ahead, but it means someone mounted. A ram-raider drives a vehicle through a shop front to steal goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram-raider is a particular kind of thief who smashes into premises with a vehicle to loot them.

clue.text: Be patronising towards women denied start

indicators.note: refused its beginning, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: discriminating against or condescending to women

explanation.surface: An instruction not to talk down to women who have been refused a head start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be' looks like a mere verb leading into an instruction, but it is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be, in its sense of having reality or life, is simply to exist.

clue.text: Agent on vacation was resting back in Crimean resort

indicators.note: going back means running in the opposite direction
a place on vacation is vacated, emptied of everything inside

parts.note: the word with its middle emptied out
past tense of lie, as in lying down to rest

explanation.surface: A spy on holiday was taking it easy at a Black Sea resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' paints a holiday, but means the word is vacated, leaving only its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta is a seaside resort town on the Crimean peninsula, famous for the 1945 Allied conference.

clue.text: Mature mother cradling son in Michelangelo's work?

parts.note: mature as in advanced in years

indicators.note: to cradle is to hold something snugly in one's arms

parts.note: Latin for mother, used in British public-school slang
the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An older mother holding her son, the subject of a Renaissance sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Pietà, Michelangelo's statue of Mary cradling Jesus. The question mark signals that his painting is an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a painting by a great European artist from before about 1800, like those Michelangelo produced.

clue.text: Find some supermarket chickens so yellow?

definitions.text: Find some supermarket chickens so yellow?

parts.note: surface reading: oven-ready birds on the shelf have had their insides removed
setter's reading: yellow is slang for cowardly, lacking courage

explanation.surface: A shopper notices the chickens in the supermarket are a yellowish colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' looks like the colour of the chicken skin, but means cowardly; oven-ready birds have literally had their insides taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking guts, or nerve, means cowardly; gutted shop poultry are literally without innards.

clue.text: Degenerate duke's command after first part of march?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to decline or get worse

definitions.text: duke's command after first part of march?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the order the Grand Old Duke of York gave once his men had marched up to the top of the hill

explanation.surface: A corrupt duke issues an order after the opening stage of a march.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme's Grand Old Duke of York marched his ten thousand men up to the top of the hill, then marched them down again.
explanation.definitionFit: To deteriorate steadily is idiomatically to slide down a slope, losing quality or health.

clue.text: Regular classes taken by inexperienced driver

parts.note: genera are classes in biological classification, plural of genus
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: Routine lessons are attended by a novice motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular classes' reads as scheduled lessons such as driving lessons, but the definition is the first word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: General and regular both mean usual or widespread, as in a general rule or regular practice.

clue.text: Men to label explosive element resistant to corrosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart so they land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Workers must mark a dangerous chemical that won't rust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive element' reads as a dangerous chemical, but the adjective belongs to the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble metals such as gold and platinum are elements that resist oxidation and attack by acids.

clue.text: Dog trained for keeping at home? Not this one

definitions.text: Dog trained for keeping at home? Not this one

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside
training reshapes something, so these letters take a new form

parts.note: taken as written
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A dog trained as a household pet, except for this wild one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: the wordplay builds a dog keeping home, while 'Not this one' says this dog is never kept as a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is Australia's wild dog, a feral canine that is not normally domesticated.

clue.text: Excessive to provoke fascist troops

parts.note: to needle is to annoy or goad
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: It is going too far to goad stormtroopers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To provoke' reads as part of a sentence but supplies a verb on its own; the SS stands for Hitler's elite troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Something excessive goes beyond what is required, so it is unnecessary or uncalled for.

clue.text: Blouses with underwear included for 14s?

indicators.note: something included is placed within the rest

parts.note: blouses are garments for the upper body, and a three-letter word for one is wanted
bras are items of women's underwear

explanation.surface: A shop offers blouses with lingerie thrown in, in dress size 14.
explanation.walkthrough: '14s' looks like a clothing size, but it refers to the answer to 14 Across. 'With' here is part of the indicator phrase rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Generals are the highest-ranking officers, collectively called the top brass in military slang.

clue.text: See 22
See 18
Possibly wise move to drop very sorrowful expression

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the letters
to drop something is to let it fall away and leave it out

parts.note: taken as written
V is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Perhaps it's prudent to stop pulling such a sad face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expression' suggests a look on the face, but here it is a phrase that is uttered. 'Possibly' at the front governs the letters left after the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is me is an old-fashioned exclamation of grief or self-pity, a phrase voicing sorrow.

clue.text: Attendant checks returning dread in two ways

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: ST for street and RD for road, two kinds of way

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so read from the end

parts.note: awe is reverential fear or dread

explanation.surface: A doorman keeps fear under control on his way back, in two directions.
explanation.walkthrough: ST and RD are the address abbreviations for street and road, both roads or ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an attendant on a ship, aircraft or at an event, who looks after passengers or guests.

clue.text: Set eyes on article in stew

parts.note: to set eyes on something is to see it
the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone spots an item floating in a casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' looks like a dish to find things in, but it is a verb meaning to fume.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew is to fret or fume angrily, and to seethe is to be inwardly furious.

clue.text: A mongrel had to be ordered to cover king in blanket

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: covering something wraps around it, enclosing it
putting things in order rearranges them into a new sequence

parts.note: a mongrel is a mix of breeds, and the word for such a hybrid follows the A
taken as written
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A mutt had to be told to lie under the monarch's blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' sounds like a command to the dog, but it signals rearranging the letters of 'had to be', which then wrap around the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanket as an adjective means applying to everyone without exception, just as an across-the-board measure does.

clue.text: Torment tiresome sort outside electronic plant

indicators.note: being outside means standing just beyond, next to rather than within

parts.note: hell is torment or agony
E as in e-mail, short for electronic
a bore is a tedious person

explanation.surface: A dull person tormenting someone outside, next to an electrical factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory making electronics, but it is a flower; 'outside' just places the dull person beyond the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellebores are a genus of flowering plants, including the Christmas rose.

clue.text: Horseless champion succeeded in love

parts.note: a champion is a hero
a deletion: horse is slang for heroin, whose abbreviation H is the letter removed, since '-less' means without
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A rider without a mount found success in romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horseless champion' suggests a dismounted knight, but horse is drug slang for heroin, whose symbol H is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love and desire, and his name also stands for erotic love itself.

clue.text: Brontë heroine reserves island home for birds

indicators.note: to reserve something is to keep it held back within

parts.note: Jane Eyre, title heroine of Charlotte Brontë's novel
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A Victorian novel's heroine books a remote island refuge for birdwatching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserves' looks like booking, but it means keeping something held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the nest of an eagle or other bird of prey, built high on a cliff or tree.

clue.text: Works from Sturluson in numbered days

indicators.note: the letters sit in the following words, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: The writings of an Icelandic author belong to a limited period.
explanation.walkthrough: Snorri Sturluson was a 13th-century Icelandic scholar whose Prose Edda preserves Norse mythology.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a collection of Old Norse literary works, and the Prose version was written by Snorri Sturluson.

clue.text: See! That catches animal!

indicators.note: to catch something is to trap it inside one's grip

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or see
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: An excited cry pointing out that something has trapped a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catches' does double duty: it describes the rope and signals that one piece holds another, so the clue is nearly all definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a rope with a running noose used by cowboys to catch cattle and horses.

clue.text: Went through stop light rounding car on late trip?

indicators.note: to round something is to go all the way about it

parts.note: red is the traffic light that means stop
a funeral car carrying the late, that is the dead

explanation.surface: A motorist jumped a red light, overtaking a car out on a late-night journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went through' sounds like running a light, but it is the definition; 'late' means dead, not after hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through a speech or play is to practise it, which is what rehearsing means.
